chapter: Pee Wee Russell and going solo
title: Sober Pee Wee as a lucid painter
summary: Freeman says painting required Pee Wee to be sober, and phoning him he sounded so articulate that he thought it was a wrong number.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But to get back to Pee Wee, I want to tell you that when Pee Wee began to paint -- you see, Pee Wee, I am sorry to say, was pretty much smashed most of his life playing -- had to, he was terribly nervous, and he could manage to play, but when it came to painting, he realized that one had to be cold sober in order to paint and he was, and I called him up one day not knowing that he was painting and he was so articulate and lucid that I thought I had the wrong party. I thought I had the wrong number.
He said, 'Oh, hello,' because he was a very bright guy, very sensitive, bright guy. It was a pity, but there again was a man who burned himself out, lived a thousand years in
the sixty-odd years he lived, you know.
